indication: [AGE]-year-old [GENDER] with right upper quadrant pain and elevated liver enzymes. History of gastric bypass. Evaluate for biliary obstruction.
technique: ** Multiplanar, multisequence MR imaging of the abdomen was performed, including dedicated MRCP sequences. T1 and T2 weighted images were obtained along with fat-saturated sequences.
findings:
**
The liver demonstrates normal morphology and signal intensity. There is no focal mass or suspicious lesion identified within the hepatic parenchyma. The portal vein and hepatic veins are patent without evidence of thrombosis. A small, simple cyst is noted in segment IV, measuring approximately 8 mm, which is an incidental finding.
The gallbladder is present but appears contracted. There are several small gallstones within the gallbladder lumen. The intrahepatic bile ducts are mildly dilated, particularly in the right lobe. The common hepatic duct is also moderately dilated. In the distal aspect of the common bile duct, there is a well-defined, rounded filling defect measuring 9 mm, consistent with an obstructing gallstone located at the level of the lower CBD. This results in upstream dilatation of the biliary tree.
Regarding the surgical history, the gastric bypass anatomy is noted, with a small gastric pouch and a Roux-en-Y limb configuration. The bowel loops visualized within the field of view show no evidence of mechanical obstruction or abnormal wall thickening.
The pancreas is normal in size and contour with no focal lesions or signs of pancreatitis. The splenic vein and artery are unremarkable. The spleen is normal in size.
The adrenal glands are unremarkable. Both kidneys demonstrate normal cortical thickness and excretion, though there is a tiny, non-obstructing 3 mm calculus in the left lower pole. No hydronephrosis is seen. There is no free fluid or lymphadenopathy identified in the peritoneum.
conclusion:
**
Obstructing gallstone in the distal common bile duct with associated intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary dilatation. No evidence of acute cholecystitis or cholangitis.
